title: The Shortest Path for a Car That Only Goes Forward: Dubins Paths, an Exact Finish for the Search, and the Loop to a Goal Just Behind You

questions.question: How many words can the shortest path of a forward-only car be?
options: Two: a left turn and a right turn
Six: LSL, RSR, LSR, RSL, RLR, LRL
Three, one for each piece
As many as there are pairs of poses
questions.explanation: Each of the three pieces is a left arc, a right arc or a straight, and only six combinations can be shortest. The method tries all six and keeps the shortest that exists.

questions.question: Over 200 pairs of poses the walked end was within:
options: 0.073 m of the goal
A centimetre of the goal
The grid's cell size of the goal
0.000000000 m of the goal
questions.explanation: Each formula was checked by driving its three pieces with exact arcs and seeing where they end. A sign error would have ended somewhere else.

questions.question: A Dubins tail after the search was how long?
options: 0.073 m, the gap it closed
4.70 m, ending exactly on the goal
It could not be built: the goal was too close
questions.explanation: The goal was a little behind and to the side of the search's last pose, so a forward-only car had to loop. From an earlier pose of the search a tail of 1.25 m was found.

questions.question: A radius of 0.4 m for this car gave a curvature of:
options: 1.35 per metre, the limit
0.40 per metre
2.50 per metre, past the limit
0.74 per metre
questions.explanation: The curvature is one over the radius. The car's smallest radius is 0.742 m, and a path drawn at 0.4 m asks for almost twice what it can steer.

questions.question: Why is the path to a goal 0.5 m behind a loop?
options: The car cannot reverse in a Dubins path: it was 10.3 times the distance
The formula is inexact for short distances
The radius was set too small
The goal's heading was reversed
questions.explanation: A car that only goes forward has to go round to arrive facing the same way half a metre back. One that could reverse would back up.

questions.question: What does the Dubins lesson not do?
options: Give the six words in closed form
Walk the path to check its end
Use the car's own radius
Check the path against the grid, or reverse
questions.explanation: The tail is geometry only. A tail that passes through a wall is possible here, and a family with reversing is another lesson.
